title: quantization-nan-debug-scratchpad-maya-2026-03-10
content:
Context:
- Investigating NaNs / quality regressions when running quantized variants of the 13B model on RTX A6000 pools. Main suspects: int8 kernel, asymmetric quantization, FP8 conversion path, KV cache accumulation, and some aten ops that get fused differently.

Summary so far:
- FP32 baseline: clean, no NaNs, logits and loss are stable across seeds.
- BF16 run: matches FP32 within expected noise.
- INT8 run (existing quantization pipeline): intermittent NaN spikes after ~200 tokens for some prompts; seems workload-dependent (long context + certain token sequences).
- FP8 experiments (experimental kernel): lower memory, similar throughput to int8, but also shows NaN cases in ~10% of validation prompts.

Environment:
- runtime: redwood-runtime v2.13.4 (local dev image)
- cuda: 12.1
- pytorch: 2.2.1
- kernels: custom int8 kernels built with CUTLASS+TVM (branch: quant-int8-stable)
- hardware: RTX A6000 (driver 535.54)
- model: redwood-open-13b-v1 (fp32 checkpoint)
- quant pipeline: calibrate -> per-tensor symmetric for weights, per-channel scale for attention q/k/v linear? (notes below)

Commands tried (local repro):
- reproducible script run:
  python experiments/run_quant_repro.py --model redwood-open-13b-v1 --quant int8 --batch 1 --seq 2048 --prompt-file test_prompts/long-context.txt --seed 42 --device cuda:0

- quick FP8 test:
  python experiments/run_quant_repro.py --model redwood-open-13b-v1 --quant fp8 --backend tvm_fp8 --seq 1024

- run with logging hooks to dump activations when NaN detected:
  export REDWOOD_DEBUG_DUMP=1; python experiments/run_quant_repro.py --quant int8 --trace-nans --dump-dir /tmp/nan_dumps

Observed error snippets (captured logs):
- "RuntimeWarning: invalid value encountered in true_divide" (numpy) at calibrate.py:147
- Kernel crash (CUDA): "cuBLAS status: CUBLAS_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR" shortly before NaN spike
- Runtime log: "Step 215: loss=nan, logits max=nan, logits min=nan, kv_cache_norm=inf"
- Activation dump (layer 18): max=3.4e+38, min=-3.4e+38, mean=1.2e+10 -> looks like overflow in softmax precompute?
- Stack trace when trace-nans on: shows NaN first appears after fused_attention_forward() return (layer 17)

Hypotheses (ordered by my current belief):
1) Quantization scale overflow in attention projection -> extremely large pre-softmax logits -> softmax numerical overflow -> NaN. (evidence: huge activation magnitudes in some layers)
2) KV cache accumulation precision drift: repeated cache updates in int8/FP8 degrade representable range causing inf/NaN downstream. (evidence: happens more for long-context sequences).
3) Asymmetric per-tensor quantization on some weight matrices causing bias accumulation during matmul -> unstable activations for specific token sequences.
4) A kernel fusion in the int8 path reorders ops and changes numeric stability (e.g., fusing dropout+add residual incorrectly).
5) Bug in TVM/FP8 custom conversion path that maps certain NaN-producing float patterns to huge exponent FP8 values.

Investigations done and quick notes:
- Re-ran failing prompt with manual clamp after matmul (clip activations to +/-1e4) -> avoids NaN and output seems reasonable (but this is a bandaid). Suggests overflow at matmul/linear output.
- Switched int8 symmetric -> int8 asymmetric per-channel for attention q/k/v; failure rate dropped but not eliminated.
- Run with mixed-precision intermediate (accumulate in bf16 for matmuls) -> mitigates NaNs entirely in local tests. Suggests accumulation precision is important.
- Added checks: after each linear, compute max(abs(.)) and if > thresh (1e3) -> log and dump. Pattern: spikes occur in softmax pre-logits in middle layers.
- Rebuilt kernels without fusion flags (disable fusions) -> reduced incidence of NaN by ~60%.
- Cross-check with CPU (float32) using same input: no NaNs. Cross-check with bf16 accumulation on GPU: no NaNs.

Data dumps (examples saved in /tmp/nan_dumps):
- dump_prompt_215_layer17_pre_softmax.npy (shape [1,161,161]) -> contains infs and extreme values.
- dump_weights_layer17_qkv_int8_scale.json -> per-channel scales show some very small scales (~1e-6) for some channels -> leads to huge dequantized weights.

Immediate actionable experiments (next):
- Add safe dequantization: dequant = int8 * scale; if scale < 1e-4 then skip int8 and use bf16 for that channel (fallback). Evaluate perf impact.
- Force bf16 accumulation for matmuls in attention (accumulate in bf16 instead of fp32) and benchmark both perf and NaN incidence.
- Re-run calibration with outlier clipping: clip activations at 99.999th percentile before computing scales. See if scales become less extreme.
- Add per-channel scale floor during calibration (min_scale = 1e-3).
- Add unit test that runs long-context prompt and asserts no NaNs for 2048 seq (run nightly on cluster).
- Create minimal reproducer that isolates single layer (layer 17) using its weights and a subsequence, run matmul dequant path to reproduce overflow deterministically.

Notes for kernel/ops owners:
- When disabling fusions we see fewer NaNs -> possibly fusion incorrectly assumes safe reorder. Tagging @Arman for kernel sanity checks on int8 fused attention path.
- Investigate how KV cache update is quantized: we store int8 compressed caches currently; consider storing bf16 or applying periodic re-scaling.

Open questions:
- Is the calibration dataset missing rare tokens that trigger extreme activations? (We used subset of training corpus, need to enlarge with adversarial tokens).
- Are there legacy clips in the codebase assuming symmetric quantization which break asymmetric flows?
- Does CuBLAS internal error indicate GPU hardware/driver flakiness? (low confidence; reproducible on multiple machines)

Quick checklist (tracking):
- [x] Reproduce locally with seed 42
- [x] Dump activations when NaN detected
- [x] Identify layer most commonly failing (layer 17/18)
- [ ] Add per-channel scale floor in calibration (experiments queued)
- [ ] Implement safe-dequant fallback for tiny scales
- [ ] Create minimal reproducer for layer 17
- [ ] Add nightly test and monitor alerts

Hypothesis validation logs (short):
- running with "--accumulate-bf16" -> 0/50 failures (good)
- calibration with 99.9 pct clipping -> reduced extreme scales but still rare tiny scales present
- per-channel asymmetric quant -> fewer NaNs but still occasionally fails (~1/20)

Attachments / where to look:
- /tmp/nan_dumps/* (see dump_* files above)
- github PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/781 (int8 kernel fixes)
- JIRA: JIRA-MLINF-482 (incident ticket)

Next steps (priority):
1) Implement scale floor + outlier clipping in calibration and run validation suite on 500 prompts (regression check).
2) Add bf16 accumulation path and perf/run impacts (if perf hit acceptable, consider as default for attention).
3) Work with kernel team to audit fused attention reorder (Arman to investigate).
4) If KV cache is stored int8, try storing bf16 with quantized storage for older layers only.

Notes to self: keep this doc informal, iterate. If we land on per-channel min-scale or bf16 accumulation, update confluence page and add config flags for Dedicated/Private customers so they can toggle quantization fallback.

Scratch command snippets for experiments:
- run calibration with clip:
  python quant/compute_scales.py --model redwood-open-13b-v1 --clip-pct 99.999 --out scales/clipped-scales.json

- run with per-channel fallback (dev flag):
  REDWOOD_QUANT_SAFE_FLOOR=1e-3 python experiments/run_quant_repro.py --quant int8 --safe-floor

- benchmark perf (compare bf16 accumulation):
  python benchmarks/throughput.py --model redwood-open-13b-v1 --quant int8 --accumulate-bf16 --batch 4 --seq 1024 --runs 30

Random notes / hypotheses to revisit later:
- Maybe logits scaling before softmax needs an explicit numerically-stable shift when using int8 dequant? (we currently rely on kernel softmax implementation).
- FP8 exponent range mapping might be wrong for some dynamic ranges -> investigate fp8 library mapping tables.

-- Maya
